newsitem.title: COSTA RICA: French coffee taste trending to Arabica beans.
newsitem.headline: French coffee taste trending to Arabica beans.

text.p: French coffee tastes are gradually moving to arabica beans from traditional robusta purchases, French trade delegates said here Monday.

Jean Loup Danon, the president of the coffee union known as SNICC, told delegates at the International Coffee Week, known as Sintercafe in Spanish, that arabics now ruled the roast in France with 55 percent of the market compared to 45 percent for robusta beans. Around 20 years ago the split was 80-20 in favour of robustas.

Roger Chaudemanche, the president of France's green coffee organisation UNACAF, also concurred that of France's purchases of around five million 60-kg bags of coffee per year 55 percent were arabica beans.

He said France imported around 1 million bags from Brazil, 800,000 from the Ivory Coast, 600,000 from Colombia, 400,000 from Uganda, 300,000 from Madagascar, 220,000 from Costa Rica, 200,000 from Guatemala nd around 180,000 from Vietnam, Cameroon and Zaire.
